findings.summary: crates/athena-cli/tests/job_plan.rs is not among the reading's deliverables
findings.evidence: A change outside the listed deliverables widens the scope.

findings.summary: Only the round-1 label assertion fails under the old code; the role-order assertion does not.
findings.evidence: crates/athena-cli/tests/job_plan.rs:596-606 already asserts [Reader, Planner, Planner, Critic, Producer, Verifier] for a plan with a mechanical finding, and it passes with today's planning.rs:194-225. The old code produces that same order, so the plan is wrong to say the order assertion would fail without the change. The demonstration still works because the '## Plan under review (round 1)' assertion fails under the old code: the old critic brief prints plan.round = 2 (briefs.rs:1251). Fix: Rewrite fails_without so it names the critic prompt's round-1 label as the distinguishing assertion. Optionally also assert that only one plan record and one critique record exist (job-plan-1 and critique-1) and that critique-1 has invocation_seq set.

findings.summary: In round 2 or later, a mechanical revision brief shows only Athena's findings, not the critic findings the planner is still answering.
findings.evidence: Step 3 returns PlanRevision { previous: plan, findings: <Athena findings>, resumed_from: None }. In a round after a critic revise, the critic's findings from the previous round are not in this brief. The planner sees them only through its own last plan. Today's code (planning.rs:216 to end_round:382) has the same gap, so this is not a regression. But it can let a fix for a critic finding slip during a mechanical pass, which would cost a critic round, the thing this job is meant to stop. Fix: Keep the findings the current critic round started with and add them to the mechanical PlanRevision's findings, after Athena's own. If you leave this out, note it as a known limit in the plan's risks.

findings.summary: The plan places the revise-in-last-round and resume-seed tests in mod.rs, but they are in the CLI test file.
findings.evidence: mod.rs has only critic_soundness_tests (mod.rs:2098) that call plan_verdict. a_retry_of_a_job_stopped_in_planning_carries_the_last_critiques_findings and the cap-loop tests are in crates/athena-cli/tests/job_plan.rs:540-567 and 844. The command in the demonstration already runs --test job_plan, so the coverage is fine. Fix: Name the actual locations of these tests in the demonstration text.

summary: I read planning.rs, the plan_findings rules in admission.rs, the planner and critic brief code in briefs.rs, the test helpers in mod.rs and the planning tests in job_plan.rs. The plan fixes the round accounting at its source. Today, planning_round sends Blocker and Major plan_findings into end_round, which uses up a round (planning.rs:194-225). The plan replaces this with a RoundEnd::Mechanical variant, an inner loop capped by a named constant, MAX_MECHANICAL_PASSES, and a separate stop reason. Keeping that reason apart from PLANNING_CAP_REASON stops planning_resume_seed from treating a plan the critic never reviewed as a seed. The code the plan names exists: plan_round, planning_round, end_round, RoundEnd, stop_planning, findings_line, base_script, athena_with, the produce_and_verify_order_tests module and repo(). The bad-plan rule also exists: the 'already exists in the base' check at admission.rs:254. Not filing mechanical attempts as records is safe for record naming, because records are keyed by job dir and round (records.rs:2763) and the check only requires round ≥ 1. Under the old code, criterion 2's demonstration fails on the count of three critic calls and criterion 3's fails on the planner-call count and the reason. Criterion 1's fails on the round-1 label, though not on the role order the plan also cites. The edit to job_plan.rs is forced: four critique_at(…, 1) assertions at lines 607, 656, 750 and 798 expect a critique with no critic call. The plan flags this openly, which answers Athena's own minor finding. No athena.toml field is added. The work fits one producer run. The remaining findings are minor, so I accept the plan.
